translation.text:
<meta>Pothi-format leaf printed in red ink. The main Uighur-Mongolian text was not transcribed by OCR, so the only translatable text is the Chinese marginal label. The 諸品經 (Zhu pin jing, "Sutra of the Various Sections") is a Chinese designation used in Beijing-printed Mongolian Kanjur volumes for the miscellaneous sutra section. The upper-left corner of the leaf is cut off at an angle. There are small cracks in the lower margin.</meta>

<margin><unclear>short Mongolian marginal label (about 4 words, likely title/volume/leaf designation), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<unclear>about 25 lines of Uighur-Mongolian script text, not transcribed</unclear>

<margin>Sutra of the Various Sections, Volume Seven, Part One, Leaf 2 <note>original: "諸品經第七卷上二" (Zhu pin jing di qi juan shang er). In Beijing imprints of the Mongolian Kanjur, this Chinese label names the section, the volume and the leaf number so that binders and readers could keep the loose leaves in order.</note></margin>

<note>A double-ruled frame printed in red surrounds the text block. Its border is a continuous scrolling design of clouds and vines. Narrow panels at the left and right edges hold the marginal labels, with cloud-scroll ornaments at the top and bottom of each panel.</note>

<summary>This is leaf 2 of the first part of volume seven of the "Sutra of the Various Sections," a section of a red-ink Mongolian Kanjur print. The main Mongolian text was not transcribed, so only the Chinese marginal label identifying the volume and leaf could be translated.</summary>
<keywords>Zhu pin jing, Sutra of the Various Sections, Mongolian Kanjur, Uighur-Mongolian script, pothi format, red-ink print, Beijing imprint, marginal label, Buddhist canon, volume seven</keywords>
